text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Syrian Vice President Abdel-Halim khaddam hands a message from President Hafez al-Assad to Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on the situation in the Middle East. Aznar says Israel's return of the Syrian lands is the basis for peace.
- Arabs satisfied with the decisions of the Arab League to halt normalisation of ties with Israel and enforce the economic boycott.
- Syrian cabinet discusses law on scientific research and the situation of winter crops and water storage.
- Arab League informs the United Nations of halting normalisation of ties with Israel.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak says Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lies, sabotages the peace process and is leading the region to a dangerous situation.
- The state-owned Syrian Commercial Bank lends one billion syrian pounds to the General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) to buy fertilizers.

- The general assemblies of the joint Syrian-Libyan companies discuss the financial situation of the companies. Syrian Finance Minister Khaled Mahayni says there are new investments for the agricultural development company.
- Four Palestinians martyred and 43 wounded in the continous clashes in the occupied Arab lands. Palestinians hold Israel responsible for the two explosions in Gaza.
- Syrian Defence Minister Lieutenant-General Mustafa Tlas and Lieutenant-General Hikmat Shihabi discuss cooperation with chief of staff of Pakistan's army Farouq Fayrouz Khan.
- Israel renews aggressions on south Lebanon.

- Head of the Syrian People's Assembly (parliament) Abdel-Qader Qaddoura discusses with the leader of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine George Habash the situation in the region and Israel's settlement policy in Jerusalem.

- The Syrian parliament discussions show that Syria in the year 2011 will need three million job opportunities and annual investment of around $3 billion. Gulf Arab countries had approvals for investments worth $1.35 billion, but then withdrew. Syria should have a money market and improve foreign trade laws to enhance investments and production process.
($1 = 50 syrian pounds in the black market)
